mu_name_from: MuProtocol/Items.cs and the old client's MuWeapons.cs both name spear group index 7 the Berdysh against Item/Spear08.bmd. The client's own enum agrees: MODEL_BERDYSH = MODEL_SPEAR + 7, and MODEL_SPEAR + i loads Spear{i+1}.
why_this_one:
The Lorencia guard's weapon, and the reason he is built at all. Five Berdysh Guards stand in the town - openmu's spawn table gives them tiles 131,88 / 173,125 / 94,125 / 94,130 / 131,148 - and the client hands each one MODEL_BERDYSH in CreateMonster. A guard without his polearm is most of a guard missing: the shaft is taller than he is and it is what reads at fifty metres, before the plate does.

It is also the first weapon here built for somebody rather than for the stance table. The Battle Axe, the Dragon Lance and the Great Scythe were each chosen to prove a row of MuWeapons.cs; this one is chosen because a named character in a named town carries it.

stats.note: The item's own row, which is what decides the damage, the swing rate and who is allowed to hold it. Copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, so the call it came from is written out beside it and the two can be read against each other in one glance.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Weapons.cs. The 0.75 table, not Season 6's - the two agree on this row and disagree on others, and 0.75 is the version this server is being built to.
stats.drop_level_note: The lowest monster that may leave this, and whether one ever does. Both are already in the call above and were being read past: the bool before the name is dropsFromMonsters and the int after it is the drop level. They are lifted out here because the loot pool is now the built catalogue gated by this number - see shared/Loot.cs. Arrows, bolts and scrolls are shop stock in the original and fall from nothing, which is what the flag says and why a spider cannot leave a quiver.
stats.width_note: width is carried because it is where OpenMU keeps two-handedness: `if (group < Bows && width == 2)` sets IsTwoHandedWeaponEquipped. It is not read as the two_handed flag above - that one is the client's, out of MuWeapons.cs - but the two must agree, and a row where they do not is a transcription error caught for free.
stats.height_note: Height is the sixth argument of the call above and was not carried across when this row was first transcribed - see width_note, which explains why width was. Both are needed now that the bag has a footprint: an item occupies a rectangle of the inventory grid rather than one cell, so a Small Axe is one across and three down, and drawing it in a single square is what made every weapon read as a thumbnail. See Satchel.Covered, which walks the rectangle.
stats.attack_speed_note: attack_speed is a stat and not a rate. OpenMU adds it whole to the character's AttackSpeed - `AttackSpeed += 1 * AttackSpeedByWeapon` in CharacterClassInitialization - and the client then spends that as `PlaySpeed = base + AttackSpeed * 0.004` on the attack action. So a weapon makes its own animation run faster, and the swing rate follows from the animation. The Kris at 50 is more than twice the Small Axe at 20 and it is visible in the arm.
stats.skill_note: The skillNumber of the call. There are no skills in this simulation, so it is carried for the row to read against the call it came from and nothing more - and it is the reason this item is dearer in the original than the price MU2 charges, since OpenMU multiplies a skilled item's price by two and a half. See shared/Market's remarks.

stance_from: ZzzCharacter.cpp's SetPlayerStop, directly: the named Spear and Dragon Lance take PLAYER_STOP_SPEAR and every other two-handed weapon in the spear group falls through to PLAYER_STOP_SCYTHE. The Berdysh is in that fall-through, which is the Great Scythe's stance - actions 7 and 20.
stance_note: Which the guards standing in Lorencia mostly do not use. SetPlayerStop tests the safe zone before it tests the weapon: inside one, everybody stands in PLAYER_STOP_MALE whatever they are holding. Four of the five Berdysh Guards stand outside Lorencia's safe zone and take the scythe stance; the fifth, at 131,148, is inside it and stands bare-handed's idle with a polearm in his fist. See the guards' own asset notes.
two_handed_from: MuWeapons.cs, TwoHanded: true, and openmu's own item table gives it the 2x4 inventory footprint every two-handed polearm in the group has. The client needs the same fact from a different direction - SetPlayerStop reads ItemAttribute[].TwoHand to choose between the sword and the scythe stance - and both say the same thing.
sheet_from: Data/Item/Polearms04.OZJ (128x32), from MuMain. The .bmd names Polearms04.jpg.
sheet_note:
remaster_one's copy is 256x64, exactly 2x - the fourth weapon running to carry that signature, after the Battle Axe, the Dragon Lance and the Great Scythe. MuMain's is the art.

A wide, short sheet rather than a square one: 128x32 is four tiles side by side, which is what a polearm needs and what none of the other three had. The blade takes the left half at something close to its real proportions and the socket and its spikes take the right.

islands.note: the shaft, the whole length of the weapon between the two heads and the largest area on it. A graded grey pole with the highlight painted down its middle - forged rather than ground, which is the Battle Axe's and the Great Scythe's shaft again and settled the same way.

the upper head: a broad axe blade with a dark back and a white ground face, twenty-four triangles reaching to the top of the model. A cutting edge, which is the one thing on this weapon blade steel is actually for.
the bright collar under the upper head, ten triangles of ring four units tall. A cast ferrule where the head is socketed onto the shaft.
the dark collar below it, the same ring at half the value. See the open question: this is the piece the sheet will not settle.

the lower head, and the reason this is a two-ended weapon rather than an axe on a pole. Identical to island 1 to the last of its 1714.7 units of area - MU built it as one head mirrored, and the two islands sample the same region of the sheet.
the bright collar above the lower head. Island 2 mirrored.
the dark collar above that. Island 3 mirrored.

material_note:
Steel throughout, in two finishes, and the teal is filler.

Sampled the way the Dragon Lance taught and the Great Scythe confirmed: every triangle at its own UV centre rather than by island bounding box, because two of these islands span 0.18 to 0.95 across the sheet and a box that wide says nothing. All seven come back neutral - the largest colour spread in the mean of any island is nine, against the Great Scythe's eleven, which is the same noise. Nothing on the model samples the cyan at all: Polearms04 is filler between its pieces exactly as Polearms05 is.

So the split is the one the other polearms made. The two heads are ground and take steel; the shaft and the four collars are forged or cast and take plate_steel.
open_question:
The four collars are one ring drawn twice at different values, and the sheet will not say which reading is right. Islands 2 and 5 sample a mean of about 130 and islands 3 and 6 about 40 - the same cylindrical fitting, one bright and one nearly black, sitting side by side on the sheet with the teal between them. Either MU drew a steel ferrule and a blackened one, or it drew the same ferrule lit and in shadow, and at 128x32 there is nothing in the pixels that decides it.

Both take plate_steel here, which is the safe way to be wrong: if they are two metals the model loses a distinction worth about twenty triangles, and if they are one metal shaded, giving the dark pair wrought_iron would have invented a material out of MU's painted shadow. wrought_iron is the candidate if anybody ever settles it - 'bar iron drawn out under a hammer and left to weather black' is what a dark ferrule on a polearm is.
